title: Gen Z demonstrations turn to evening riots and looting in German cities
seoTitle: Frankfurt Gen Z protests and evening riots

tea.why: Young people protested against rising living costs, a deteriorating education system, inadequate housing markets, and military conscription.

tea.changed: Nov 1: Police reported numerous arrests, including over 30 individuals in Frankfurt, following evening clashes and looting.

summary: Mass demonstrations organised by the initiative “Gen Z regelt” took place across multiple German cities, including Frankfurt, Berlin, Hamburg, and Cologne. While afternoon rallies largely proceeded peacefully with thousands of participants gathering near rivers and public squares, events turned violent after nightfall. Rioters clashed with police, set fire to barricades, launched fireworks and Molotov cocktails, and looted businesses, including a gun shop in Frankfurt where weapons were briefly stolen. The initiative stated its goal was to amplify youth voices on key issues like education, climate, and the rising cost of living, while disclaiming violence. Authorities deployed water cannons and heavy police presences to manage the unrest, resulting in dozens of arrests and some injuries among officers.
demands: Better education and more money for schools
Affordable housing and solutions to the housing crisis
response: Police deployed water cannons, blocked major shopping streets, and made dozens of arrests after clashes and looting broke out. Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt characterized the rioters as left-wing groups and chaos-makers from a migrant background.

updates.text: Afternoon demonstrations involving thousands of young people took place across various German cities.
As night fell, protests escalated into riots, store looting, and clashes with police in Frankfurt, Cologne, Hamburg, and Berlin.
Frankfurt police blocked Die Zeil, used water cannons, and arrested over 30 people following widespread looting and a break-in at a gun shop.
